steps.name: Sea Patrol Captain
steps.text: There you are, Consul Clementia.

steps.name: Sea Patrol Captain
steps.text: We noticed an extremely unusual bio-signature in the Sophontheatrum. I'm glad you're unharmed.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: What's the status of the frontline?

steps.name: Sea Patrol Captain
steps.text: Legions VIII and X, alongside the Sea Patrol, have been sending out escort ships alternatively, as per your orders.

steps.name: Sea Patrol Captain
steps.text: The city's reorganization and the force fields are both complete. Milliarium is holding against the Seaborn tide.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Inform every relevant researcher in the city. I need a minute-by-minute breakdown of the situation of this region of sea.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: We're still being far too passive even with our contingency plan put into motion.

steps.name: Sea Patrol Captain
steps.text: Madame Consul, you may want to see what the drone matrix just sent back.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: These passages of light between the Seaborn...

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: 'Waterways'?

steps.name: Ægir Technician
steps.text: Consul Clementia, we've re-established communication with the home territories! We just got a dispatch from the Institute of Scientific Development Planning.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Any news from the Hunters?

steps.name: Sea Patrol Captain
steps.text: Three of them have returned to Milliarium. They're cleaning up the remaining Seaborn in the eastern city units.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Contact Gladiia. Tell her to come meet us immediately.

steps.name: Sea Patrol Captain
steps.text: Yes, Madame Consul.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Let's go, Kal'tsit, Doctor.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: You need to deepen your contact with Ægir.

options: I'll go with this captain to inform the Hunters.
Kal'tsit alone will be enough for diplomacy.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: (Whisper) Doctor?

options: (Whisper) That Seaborn left and head to the east...
(Whisper) That Seaborn might run into Skadi...

steps.text: You exchange a quick glance with Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Madame Consul, the Doctor still has some affairs to settle.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: ...Very well.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The final battle for the Waterway Program has concluded with a Seaborn invasion of Milliarium. I require an explanation, Consul Clementia.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Gladiia.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Were any of you harmed?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I see you're here too, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We had a few unexpected encounters, but nothing we couldn't handle.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I believe that, as an envoy of Iberia, Dr. Kal'tsit also requires an explanation.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I could use one myself, if we're being honest.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: There is someone who wishes to see you all.
The Little Handy moves to the center of the Pensivarium, its projection module emitting cold motes of light, slowly coalescing into the figure of an Ægir woman.
She sports a smile under her golden hair. Her eyes are focused on everyone in the room, as though she has been waiting for, or perhaps observing, them for a long time.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Consul Horatia.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Whyever do you look so fatigued, my little Gladiia?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Though the transmission efficiency of the Waterway is much higher than I anticipated, I fear our simulacra are still unable to transmit my feelings.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Otherwise I'd stroke your hair and give you a nice, big hug.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: No need. You know the risks of doing so.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The changes on the sea's surface, as well as the sudden appearance of the 'Waterways'. Was this your doing?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Whether Ægir or Seaborn, we all find ourselves competing over time.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: The Seaborn must keep sending nutrients to every region of sea they conquer. They wish to quickly transform the entire continental shelf into one great nest.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Every issue has two sides. This disaster has also blessed us with bio-energy beyond measure.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: More than two centuries ago, the beacon launcher would have required a dozen cities' bio-energy systems to continually fabricate the nanomachines comprising the Waterways.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Now, those nanomachines are being fostered by the Seaborn, who regard them as harmless kin.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Using the data flow between the nanomachines as a medium, fleets and cities in squeezed state could traverse the oceans in an instant.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Though these machines cannot take Ægir to the stars as our forebears imagined, they are more than enough to carve a path of life for civilization in its time of need.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: But that would mean that, for the foreseeable future, Ægir will have no choice but to enter into some kind of symbiosis with the Seaborn, using that... scum, as they in turn use us.

spans.text: But that would mean that, for the foreseeable future, Ægir will have no choice but to enter into some kind of
with the Seaborn, using that... scum, as they in turn use us.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Is this another of your so-called 'games'?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: It is how we will break through this siege.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: The term 'Waterway,' the path ahead for Ægir, has never referred only to pure waters.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: You have always had your doubts about the Program, and that is fine. But if that doubt serves only to put you in disarray, then it is useless.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: As Ægir is determined to open a Waterway between sea and land, there was no question that it shall do so.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I do not doubt your success, but perhaps there is still room for debate as to your methods.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tist, I presume. Consul Horatia, of the Institute of Scientific Development Planning. It's a pleasure.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: It pleases me that there are still those on dry land who have inherited the will of the prehistoric civilization. That Ægir is not alone in our duty.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: I am also glad to see you have begun our discussion with a firm diplomatic stance.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Then can I take it that you speak for all terrestrial civilizations, and that we can dispense with establishing diplomacy with them one by one?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I, too, am glad to see Ægir abandon its contentment in isolation and seek out cooperation with the land.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But I regret to inform you, Madame Consul, that I do not represent it in its entirety. I merely understand it more than most.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That said, I believe what Ægir needs now is exactly a thorough understanding of the terrestrial civilizations.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You and I both know that this Waterway will not be used only for resisting the Seaborn. Ægir has its eyes on every unnatural existence in these lands.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: It is the only means for us to ascertain the intrinsic nature of Terra, and to eliminate the disasters hanging above our heads at the source.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And I am sure you are aware of how such actions will be perceived by the terrestrial nations.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Compared to the Seaborn, you would be seen as the more direct threat.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: We bear them no ill will. We need not stoop so low.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: The cruelest thing we could do is ignore the need of help of other tottering civilizations we meet on the road to settling this crisis.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Of course, we will first help them to learn how to walk.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Bottlenecks of development, dilemmas of war, barriers of race, clashes of cultures, trends of ideology, changes in the structure of society...

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Over the millennia, Ægir has grown freely beneath the waves. It has faced every issue a country might face.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: We wish to share our experiences, without reservation.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And how would you do so?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Using Milliarium as our main port, we would send talent and technology ashore, to aid the Iberians in revitalizing their home.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Feranmuts perceive the oncoming crisis far more keenly than humanity. That young one will not shelter Kjerag forever.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: We can aid that nation long trapped in snow in breaking through its developmental barriers in a few short years, so that it may stand equal with its neighbors.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: We can aid the Sami in purging the demonic corruption permeating every inch of snow, and restart the abandoned stargate in the north.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Ursus? Kazdel? If the flames of war rage, we will calm them. If there are disputes, we will resolve them.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Bolívar? Higashi? National unity is but a few fruitful negotiations away.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Ægir will aid them in every predicament. Ægir will guide them towards the only goal they need. Under the leadership of Ægir, the land and sea will share a common future.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Madame Consul, I do not doubt Ægir's sincerity, but... I fear your proposals will not have the effect you expect.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I am sure you have the means to bring Kjerag up to par with the Core nations in a few years.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But will dialogues between equals necessarily center around peace and development?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Were Ursus's internal problems to be resolved, who is to say they would not bare their fangs once more, and attack their neighbors to satisfy their regained appetite?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Bolívar's many regimes might reach a consensus under Ægir's pressure, but how will you eradicate the profound, deliberately provoked hostility?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, are you saying that Ægir's efforts to aid the terrestrial civilizations will only result in the opposite?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I am saying that we can establish a more equal and profound cooperative relationship between us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: With only your probes, you are unable to understand a civilization's needs. With only your experiences, you are unable to force a nation to skip over its path to development.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Before you act, you must learn more. Otherwise, the winds you stir on land may become some great storm you cannot turn a blind eye to.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: We would be more than happy to hear your suggestions, then.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: On the condition that you do not allow us to be held back by excessive caution and meaningless apprehension.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Seeing the gulf between us, between land and sea, I understand that we will need many more discussions before we can make progress.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Once the Waterway opens, I look forward to meeting you in the flesh. Whether on land, or in Ægir's home territories.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I as well, Madame Consul.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: What about you, Gladiia?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Do you agree with Dr. Kal'tsit on this matter?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The IDP need not question Rhodes Island's sincere wish for cooperation, nor Dr. Kal'tsit's ability. I can vouch for both of those.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And there are indeed essential differences between Ægir and the nations of the land.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The land dwellers are shortsighted and clumsy, which makes them frail. Forcibly removing the differences between them would be no different from destroying them.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It is truly necessary to show good faith.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Hmm.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: I've never seen Gladiia place so much trust in someone, Dr. Kal'tsit. A feat, to be sure.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Perhaps she can be a bridge between our peoples, and aid us in coming to a consensus.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: You will see that Ægir's plans are no mere idle pratter.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Now, do allow me a moment alone with Consul Clementia.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Secunda, a fleet approaches from the land!

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Iberia.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Hail them via the drone matrix.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: This is Praefecta Secunda, of the Milliarium Sea Patrol.
Err... It's me.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Irene?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: We're currently in a head-on battle against the Seaborn. Don't come any closer.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Your ships are too crude. I'm sorry, but they may get sucked into the eddies around Milliarium.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: You're saying that Iberia should just wait quietly on land?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: That I should just watch Milliarium get invaded by Seaborn, and let the Waterway transform into some kind of god-knows-what that even you Ægir never foresaw?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: We've already talked about this, Secunda. I'll be there in five minutes.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Halt all attacks.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: If we are going to pick up the Iberians, we'll just have to open the access channels to the rear. Why stop attacking?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Look at the screen.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The Academy of Technology just sent an urgent communique.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: This...

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: What do we do?

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Are those light-emitting nanomachines components for the Waterway?

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: But the Seaborn are still attacking the city. If they've fused with the nanomachines and bear identical bio-signatures, our weapons won't be able to locate and attack the Seaborn only...

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Don't tell me the Legions want us to halt our covering fire and rely only on Milliarium's force fields to hold them back?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: May as well slit our wrists and be done with it.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Scribbling on your device again? You know, sometimes I really admire your ability to keep a cool head.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Use the images from the drone matrix to render a 3D model.

steps.name: 'Little Handy'
steps.text: Rendering in progress.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Perhaps the answer lies within the riddle itself.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The bio-signatures of the nanomachines and the Seaborn are identical, but we still know clearly that the nanomachines have formed a Waterway.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: How?

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: We can see them! Each machine emits a particular light that's clearly visible!

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Contact the Academy of Technology, and tell them we have a proposal for modifying our weapons' targeting systems.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: But... recalibrating two Legions' worth of auxiliary optical systems would take a lot of time.
What about using a lighthouse on land?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Irene.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: It seems we arrived in the nick of time. A dozen or so lighthouses on the lost coastline have resumed operation. They're... responding to your Waterway.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Combined, they should be enough to illuminate this entire patch of sea. Maybe they could serve as your auxiliary optical systems?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I'm hardly an engineer, but these lighthouses were built with Islander... er, Ægirian technology. They should be compatible with your existing systems.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: That should cut the time needed in half. I'll let Consul Clementia know.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: ...Thank you, Irene.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: The Inquisition would be overjoyed to see these newly unclouded Eyes become part of the combined defenses of land and sea. We're partners now, Secunda.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Though maybe we should be thanking Breogan instead.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Breogan...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: He truly dedicated himself to these lighthouses.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: A naval architect drifting into a foreign land, striving for the day when land and sea could work together. He foresaw calamity, but left no answers behind.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: It's a pity that Ægir saw him as an outsider, while Iberia never truly accepted him. He died alone and miserable. But now, his plans will finally have the chance to become reality.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: ...We acted far slower than he did.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: But it's not too late. Or rather, now is precisely the time.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Let's get started, Irene.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I'm still more used to you with your veil on, Horatia.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Did you show off the scar below your ear to let Gladiia know that, as her mother, you will tolerate her setbacks just as you accept the blemish she left on your face?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Hah, I'm not that strict a mother.
With her left hand on the astrolabe, Horatia's right hand softly strokes her cheek below her right ear, where a thin scar stretches upwards, nearly touching her eye.
There is a smile on her face.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: But this is no blemish. It's beautiful. Trivial for a doctor to erase, but I refuse.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: My little Gladiia was barely five at the time. She was taking her first career development assessment, and through this made her wishes rather clear.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: You don't know how glad I am to see her grown.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: She's certainly more suited for the life of a legionnaire than in the Institute of Social Planning or Institute of Scientific Development Planning like you expected.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: No matter. Whatever field she joins, she is sure to excel. She was born for Ægir.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I remember when she was two, the Institute of Incubation said your disposition and the nature of your work made you ill-suited to raise her, and suggested you place her in their care.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: They said the same when I first decided to raise her myself. Saying that again two years later would not change my mind.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: But what truly pleased me was seeing young Gladiia reject it as well.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I wouldn't say you have the best bond as mother and daughter, but you do have an odd kind of rapport.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Alright, that's enough, my little manta ray. I suspect we have more pressing matters to discuss than reminiscing about my daughter.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: ...Can you please not call me that?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Very well, Consul Clementia.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: While we spoke, every city in the home territories has been conducting an unprecedented investigation into the Church of the Deep.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: As the core of R&D, Blandus was able to tamper with the Class IV weapons, but his actions should absolutely have been detected at some point before they were put to use.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Meaning there are many behind him fanning the flames.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: All members of both Academies who had anything to do with the weapons' design, manufacture, and maintenance are receiving the most thorough investigations possible.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: In response, the Church has brought their full influence to bear. By grasping at a single leaf, we may be able to pull out an entire rotten branch.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: And with Mártus, no doubt we will be able to identify the Church's deepest roots.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: ...Ægir itself is undergoing a grand surgery.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Surgery to cut out a festering tumor. Isn't it?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: The Waterway is open, and the fallen who corrupt our nation have been revealed. Both are of great value, as I see it.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Are you trying to console me over the superficial Waterway Program's failure? To tell me that the sacrifices Milliarium made were not without meaning?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Why do you insist on double negatives? They make you seem weak.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: There is no such thing as a 'superficial' program in Ægir, Consul Clementia.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: If the IDP has approved a program, it means its planning and members are entrusted with the hopes of Ægir.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: We believed you are capable of using the Class IV weapons to purify our waters and open the Waterway. This has always been an official part of the program.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: ...Yet it failed.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: The theoretical success rate of oceanic purification was never high. However, the Waterway Program was a guaranteed success.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Did I not promise you that, before you set off? Trust in me. Trust in Ægir.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I don't doubt that even if this city were to sink, consigning all ten thousand or so Ægir souls in it to the depths, the Waterway would still open without hitch.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: However, of all the possibilities you've accounted for, how many call for sacrifice?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: How I wish this meeting of ours never had to happen, Horatia.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Is that why you've worked yourself to the bone, my little manta ray?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: I've read the reports on Milliarium. As consul for the entire city, you need not throw yourself into each and every little affair.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: The stimulants you abuse will not hide the exhaustion on your face.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: You really have thought of everything. As you always do, Horatia.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: All these losses and sacrifices, the falls and the betrayals, even Mártus's secret... Are you not the least bit shaken?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Speaking of Mártus... You've reminded me of something.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Of what?

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Mártus regards himself as the 'gardener of sin'. At times like these, he is wont to hide himself behind history.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: I can infer why he'd seek cooperation from Dr. Kal'tsit, but from the way you describe it, those 'discussions' quickly devolved into a vapid declaration of war.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: I find it difficult to imagine he would be satisfied with such a failure of negotiations. That is, unless he gained some other information...

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: We will continue to track his whereabouts.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Are you hiding something, my little manta ray?

Clementia does not answer. She instead raises her head to look at Horatia, face to face. With the simulacrum erasing the distance between them, she knows that Horatia will be able to see every detail of her expression.
But the curve of Horatia's lips do not change, her eyes are as gentle as ever, too.
Clementia hopes that her own expression is as firm as hers.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I am still the Chief Designer of Warfare on the Waterway Program before you arrive, Horatia.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Naturally.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Your calculations may have arrived at the correct outcome, but I had to handle the situation in my own way. The Academy of Science and Academy of Technology each have their own duties.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Hmm... Yes, of course.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: I only hope that this obsession with self-reflection will not cause any complications. Your keen judgment must stay unclouded.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I won't let that happen.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: *sigh* Here, come a little closer. We still have some time.

steps.name: Horatia
steps.text: Kal'tsit, Rhodes Island, Iberia, the Inquisition... You'll be busier than ever soon, so best not keep frowning like that...

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Rapidly convulses its gelatinous body)

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Quizzically sways fine tentacles)

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Trying to run?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Smart. Your kin are behind this wall. A lot of them.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's the end of the road for you, though. What a pity.
Ishar-mla?
Ishar-mla.
A sudden voice, tinged with surprise.
Skadi turns, looking towards its source. A conical creature exuding light leaves the shadows of the buildings, shielding the two cornered Seaborn with its body.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Leave, kin.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Through the eddy ahead, return to the sea.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You're so honestly gentle with them. Disgusting.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'm guessing you're the leader?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Our meeting was preordained, Ishar-mla.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Huh? You know me?
Skadi grips her sword tightly.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Ishar-mla.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: From Sal Viento to Gran Faro, from the Stultifera to here. You scum have been watching me this whole time.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What, do you see your 'god' in me too? Are you here for 'family,' or revenge?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: (The nuclei within its skull rotate slightly)

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: No.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Ishar-mla... Ska-di, you are not nutrients to complete the cycle. You are its end.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Our kin will not prey on you.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: On the contrary, they respect you. Protect you.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: They await your transformation. They await your evolution.
Skadi looks at the being's 'eye.' For whatever reason, this monster she has never seen before seems familiar. Very familiar.
The bizarre organs surrounding the Seaborn disperse and surround her in turn. A shimmering 'umbilical cord' connects her body with the Seaborn's.
Skadi suddenly remembers when she faced the first Seaborn to talk, in that cave below the church. She also experienced a moment of distraction back then.

She had just been through a fierce battle, her blood boiling with frenzy. But now, she feels herself uncontrollably responding to the Seaborn's touch... She curses herself for this moment of distraction.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...Why?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: A natural phenomenon. One I am also helpless to resist. This is the answer, Ska-di.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: I ate of His flesh, and He lives within you.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: You are He. I am He.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Our hearts connected. Our blood interlinked.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: You need not waver. You need not doubt. The kin will not demand you walk with us.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Ishar-mla chose you. Chose you to continue His life. Perhaps this is the only way He will witness what He must witness. Travel the road He must travel.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: What did He see in you?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Perhaps, perhaps...

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Could it be, Ska-di, that in that cold, dark future, in the cosmos where all things are doomed to fade away, you are the one hope, the spark, the possibility...

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Are you the one who bears the final wishes of untold lives?

options: Skadi.
Abyssal Hunter Skadi.
Rhodes Island Operator Skadi.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Doctor?
Skadi swings her sword, her grip never once relaxed. It slices through the 'umbilical cord.' She stares coldly at the creature before her.

options: Everyone's looking for you.
Figured you'd be here.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, Ska-di. You... know each other?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Is that so strange?

options: She's one of my cute little operators.
We met on land.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: (The nuclei within its chest pulse)
This is the first time something stirs the peace within the Seaborn's chest.
The oddly-colored nuclei, along with the bizarre organs floating by their side, begin to wave as rhythmically as the tides.
It does not approach, but both you and Skadi can sense a burst of emotion: joy.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: No matter if you personally took part, Dr. {@nickname}, no matter if what took place in the cerulean cave had aught to do with you...

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: After countless, countless years, you now stand alongside Ishar-mla.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The connection between you and the kin cannot be erased. It is you who wrote this instinct into our memories. We depend on one another.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The wheel of fate still turns. The surviving successors will one day meet, and achieve the most improbable of possibilities—

a.text: The hardship we suffer is ever present.
The life we thirst for is ever present.
I await you at the endpoint of evolution, Dr. {@nickname}, Ska-di. I await you both.

options: Don't give chase, Skadi.
Handle things in the city first.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I couldn't understand that thing at all. What was it talking about?

options: Some kind of declaration of war.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Didn't sound like that to me.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You woke me up just now, Doctor.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: When I was face-to-face with that Seaborn, I remembered something I felt back in Sal Viento.

options: Nothing good, I presume?
I assume you weren't a fan?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I hated it.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What good could come from a Seaborn rambling to a human?

options: Don't worry. I know what happened.
You didn't want to listen, did you?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Good. I couldn't explain even if I wanted to.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You don't seem surprised, though. No wonder Kal'tsit asked you to come underwater.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Of course not!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I have no interest in chatting with a Seaborn.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: That thing sounded like it'd been looking for you?

options: It's a long story.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...So we were both being watched.

options: There won't be a next time.
Next time, I'll be by your side.
It'll be you waking me up next time.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Don't worry, Doctor. I'm Skadi. Abyssal Hunter Skadi. Rhodes Island Operator Skadi. Always have been.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Doesn't matter if that thing comes looking for me or you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'll cut its vocal cords before it can speak.

options: I trust you, Skadi.
Remember who you are, and it'll work out.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...The tide's coming in, outside these walls.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Sounds like it won't stop for a long while.
